title.purpose: Wordmark and section headings only — the largest text in the system.

body.purpose: Default running text, labels, status messages.

small.purpose: List-row content: seeks, ratings, recent games.

numeric.purpose: Clock time only — tabular-nums, the one place weight/size step up for legibility under time pressure.

shadows.name: interactive-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover/focus/active feedback on buttons and the promotion picker only — never on a resting element. Exposed as --lift.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Background and border-color changes on inputs and small controls.

motion.name: state-lift
motion.purpose: Paired background + box-shadow transition when a button takes the Interactive Lift on hover/focus.

motion.name: text-state
motion.purpose: Color-only transitions, such as navigation link opacity/color on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every transition above is disabled under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

components.name: Button
components.description: The single button style used everywhere: sign in, register, create/cancel seek, flip board, theme toggle, sign out. There is no separate primary variant — hierarchy comes from placement and copy.
components.css: .ds-btn { font: inherit; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid currentColor; background: transparent; color: var(--fg, #bababa); cursor: pointer; transition: background 160ms ease, box-shadow 160ms ease; } .ds-btn:hover { background: var(--panel, rgba(255,255,255,0.04)); box-shadow: var(--lift, 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.28)); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--sel, #20b2aa); } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; box-shadow: none; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn { transition: none; } }

components.name: List Row
components.description: Shared row treatment for seek list, ratings list, and recent-games list. One row style for the whole app.
components.css: .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--panel, rgba(255,255,255,0.04)); font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--fg, #bababa); } .ds-row-cancel { font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 2px 10px; }

components.name: Clock
components.description: Dual-side chess clock; the side to move renders in the selection accent, reinforcing 'this is live right now' as one consistent meaning.
components.html:
White10:00
Black10:00
components.css: .ds-clock { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--panel-strong, rgba(255,255,255,0.06)); } .ds-clock-side { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; color: var(--fg, #bababa); } .ds-clock-active { color: var(--sel, #20b2aa); } .ds-clock-label { font-size: 0.75rem; opacity: 0.7; } .ds-clock-time { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Board Square (light)
components.description: Light board square with a legal-destination hint dot. The dot/ring shape difference is colorblind-relevant, not decorative. --light and --hint are defined once in :root and never remapped per theme, so the square stays the same wood tone in both themes — the token carries that constancy rather than hiding it in a literal.
components.css: .ds-sq { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-sq-light { background: var(--light, #f0d9b5); } .ds-sq-hint::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 30%; height: 30%; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--hint, rgba(20, 85, 30, 0.5)); pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Board Square (dark, selected)
components.description: Dark board square in the selected state. The ring is two-tone on purpose: board squares are theme-independent and no teal clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 against both, so a 1px ink edge carries the contrast while the teal band carries the meaning.
components.css: .ds-sq-dark { background: var(--dark, #b58863); } .ds-sq-selected { outline: 1px solid var(--sel-edge, #161512); outline-offset: -1px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--sel, #20b2aa); }

components.name: Promotion Choice
components.description: Promotion picker tile over a scrim. --promo-tile and --promo-tile-ink are defined once in :root and never remapped, so the tile stays near-white in both themes — which is why its focus ring uses Grandmaster Teal Deep: standard Teal is only 2.5:1 here, under the 3:1 floor.
components.css: .ds-promo-choice { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 48px; height: 48px; padding: 0; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--promo-tile, #fafafa); color: var(--promo-tile-ink, #111); font-size: 1.75rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 160ms ease, box-shadow 160ms ease; } .ds-promo-choice:hover { box-shadow: var(--lift, 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.28)); } .ds-promo-choice:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--sel-deep, #17827c); }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Topbar navigation link (Lobby / Profile). No underline, no pill, no tab background.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { color: var(--fg, #bababa); text-decoration: none; opacity: 0.8; transition: color 150ms ease, opacity 150ms ease; } .ds-nav-link:hover { opacity: 1; } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--sel, #20b2aa); border-radius: 6px; }

narrative.overview: Gambit's UI reads like the desk of a serious player: warm dark wood and felt, one board lit at the center, nothing else competing for attention. The palette borrows the same board-square hues generations of players already trust (Lichess and Chess.com both start here), because reinventing the board would cost recognition for no gain — the differentiation is in restraint, not novelty. Chrome is minimal to the point of being nearly invisible: no shadows at rest, no card stacks, no gradient flourishes. The one saturated color in the system, a teal, exists solely to say "this is selected, this is active, this is focused" — it is never decorative. This system explicitly rejects two aesthetics named in PRODUCT.md: the generic SaaS dashboard (cards everywhere, gradient heroes, tool-for-work chrome) and the cluttered, gamified chess site (badge walls, streak counters, noisy gamification competing with the board). Precision reads as premium here; decoration reads as noise.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black by default (#161512), with a true light mode, not a tint of the dark palette
Classic wood board coloring — familiar, not novel
One accent color, one job: interactive/selected state
Fully flat at rest; elevation appears only as a response to touch
System font stack only — clarity over typographic personality

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Grandmaster Teal is the only saturated interactive color in the system. It is never used twice for two different meanings — error state gets Ember, board feedback gets its own dedicated hues.

rules.name: The No-Hero Rule
rules.body: There is no display-scale heading anywhere in the system. The board is the largest, highest-contrast element on every screen; type never competes with it for size.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: No element carries a shadow in its default state. Shadows exist purely as interaction feedback — the instant the pointer or focus leaves, the shadow leaves with it.

dos: Do keep the board as the single largest, highest-contrast element on every screen.
Do use Grandmaster Teal for one meaning only: active/selected/focused.

Do switch to Grandmaster Teal Deep wherever the accent lands on a light surface — light theme, or the always-near-white promotion tile. This is a legibility variant of the same meaning, not a second accent; light mode remaps --sel to it automatically, so use --sel and it resolves correctly.
Do keep every list on the identical panel-row treatment.
Do reserve shadows for interaction feedback only.
Do keep legal-move/last-move/premove board cues distinguishable by shape as well as color.
Do use Ember/Ember Deep for error and danger states exclusively.
donts: Don't build a generic SaaS-dashboard look — no card grids, no gradient hero banners, no tool-for-work chrome.
Don't add gamification clutter — no badge walls, streak counters, or achievement noise.
Don't introduce a second accent color for variety.
Don't add a resting-state shadow to any card, panel, or list row.
Don't introduce a new border-radius value.

Don't reuse the dark-mode Panel Tint (a white overlay) unmodified in light mode — a white-on-near-white overlay is close to invisible on Paper. This is handled by the --panel / --panel-strong tokens, which resolve to a white overlay on Ink and an ink-tinted dark overlay on Paper; use those tokens rather than a raw rgba(255,255,255,…) fill.
Don't drop the ink edge from the board selection ring to 'clean it up' — it is what carries WCAG 1.4.11 contrast against squares no teal can clear.
